standard_prerequisites.name: Characterisation of the Chern classes by one relation on the projective bundle, and the projection formula
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-determine-intersections (proof lines 7903 and 7917) and lemma-pushforward-cap-c1 (proof line 7911)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives both the relation satisfied by the classes of F and the uniqueness that identifies the classes of E from the pushed forward relation, and the second moves the cap with a power of the first Chern class through the pushforward.

core_obligations: Reduce to an integral base and set up the projective bundles: by the vanishing criterion it suffices to compare the caps with the fundamental class when X is integral, and the surjection E -> F gives a closed immersion of the projective bundle of F into that of E over X (proof lines 7880-7891).

Realise the smaller projective bundle as a divisor with trivial normal bundle: the constant section of E gives a global section of the twisting sheaf whose zero set is exactly the image of the closed immersion, so that image is an effective Cartier divisor whose associated invertible sheaf is the twisting sheaf; consequently capping with the first Chern class of the twisting sheaf equals the pushforward of the pullback along the immersion (proof lines 7892-7902).

Compare the relations: the classes of F satisfy the relation of the characterisation lemma on the projective bundle of F; pushing that relation forward along the immersion and using the previous identification together with the projection formula produces the relation for E with the powers shifted by one, and the uniqueness part of the characterisation lemma then forces the top Chern class of E to vanish and the lower ones to equal those of F (proof lines 7903-7921).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an integral base and build the closed immersion of the projective bundles (proof lines 7880-7891).
Identify the smaller projective bundle with a divisor of trivial normal bundle (proof lines 7892-7902).
Push the characterising relation forward and conclude by uniqueness (proof lines 7903-7921).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Chern classes of a finite locally free sheaf which is an extension of a sheaf of one lower rank by the structure sheaf: the top Chern class vanishes and all the lower ones agree with those of the quotient (statement lines 7862-7878, tag 02UG). The proof is a real comparison through projective bundles: it reduces to an integral base, embeds the projective bundle of the quotient into the projective bundle of the extension, realises the smaller one as an effective Cartier divisor cut out by the constant section so that its normal bundle is trivial, and then pushes the characterising relation of the quotient forward to obtain the relation of the extension, whose uniqueness forces the claimed identifications. The pushforward of the relation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
